global_caption: The video contains 7 shots and is a realistic, cool-toned industrial tutorial-style short on electronic soldering. It progresses at a steady, reserved pace, with consistent lighting created by overhead lab lights and localized workbench illumination producing cool white shadows. Chinese The overall tone remains focused, calm, and professional.
shot1: Shot 1 opens with a direct cut, using a medium high-angle shot to capture the electronic lab workbench. The composition centers on the soldering station, iron, solder wire, desoldering pump, and circuit board. In the foreground are neatly arranged tools; the background features a blurred equipment rack. Focus is firmly on the work area. A young woman wearing an anti-static wristband places her hands at the edge of the frame to indicate the operational zone. Cool overhead lighting evenly illuminates the surface. The Chinese voiceover briefly states to confirm power is off and ensure ventilation.
shot2: Shot 2 follows with a hard cut from the previous shot, transitioning to a close-up at eye level with a slight downward angle. The shallow depth of field emphasizes the hands and soldering iron tip. In the foreground are cleaning sponge and solder wire; the background shows a blurred soldering station indicator light. The subject first cleans the pad with a tool, then lightly touches the iron tip to the solder wire to tin it. The metal surface transitions from dull to slightly reflective, with fine highlights appearing along the iron tip's edge under the cool white work lamp. The Chinese The camera performs a very slight lateral pan following hand movement from the pad to the iron tip, making the procedural relationship clear.
shot3: Shot 3 cuts hard from the previous shot, shifting to a medium-close high-angle composition. In the foreground is the resistor to be installed; the background shows blurred desk tools. The subject uses both hands to precisely insert the resistor into its corresponding hole, then flips the board over and gently presses the leads with fingers to secure position. The transition from suspended to flush-mounted component is clearly visible. Lighting remains cool and even, with only fine highlights preserved on the metallic leads. The Chinese voiceover explains confirming correct hole placement and component alignment. The camera slightly lowers and subtly pushes in to emphasize accurate insertion and rear fixation.
shot4: Shot 4 cuts hard into a critical close-up operation, using a tight shot at eye level with a slight downward angle. The composition compresses the pad, lead, iron tip, and solder wire into a single focal plane, with the background completely blurred into a cool-toned workbench. The subject first makes the iron touch both pad and lead simultaneously, then feeds solder wire from the side. The solder melts quickly, flows, and coalesces into a single smooth, full solder joint. The camera clearly captures the continuous transformation from solid to molten to solidified state. Clean reflections appear on the joint surface under the local work lamp. The Chinese The camera performs an extremely slight push-in to intensify the core technical action.
shot5: Shot 5 continues with a hard cut based on continuous motion, switching to a close-up high-angle view showing adjacent solder joints. The circuit traces form guiding lines. Focus follows the iron as it rapidly and steadily moves between multiple joints. The subject completes several adjacent joints in sequence, each with minimal dwell time. Joint shapes remain consistent with clear boundaries, no excess buildup on traces. The sleeve edge and fine wires exhibit natural, slight movement due to motion. Cool lighting maintains uniform texture.
shot6: Shot 6 cuts hard from the previous shot, transitioning to a medium-close eye-level angle. In the foreground are diagonal-cut pliers and the just-soldered underside of the board; in the background are a magnifying glass and workbench. The subject first snips off excess leads with a clean, decisive motion at the moment of metal separation, then moves the magnifying glass over the joint to check for fullness and bridging. Focus naturally shifts between snipping and inspection. The curvature, edges, and spacing of the joint surface are clearly visible. The Chinese Snipping The camera first slightly pulls back to accommodate tool motion, then slowly pushes in to reveal details under the magnifying glass.
shot7: Shot 7 concludes with a soft fade-in from the previous shot, using a medium eye-level angle facing the workbench. The composition places the circuit board slightly below center, with the power cord entering from the side to guide the viewer’s gaze. The subject connects power for testing; the indicator light stabilizes and becomes the visual focus. This small point of light stands out clearly in the cool lab environment, making the result immediately apparent, yet the overall style remains rational and controlled. She then slightly retracts her hand, leaving a clear view of the finished product and tools. The camera slowly pulls back to end, including both the successful test and the complete workbench in the frame, creating a clear, professional, credible tutorial conclusion.
